note: The adjudicator's own answer, copied from the harness's recorded result rather than retyped. Not a provenance claim: the operator runs this script and can edit the transcript. It exists so the judge's answer is committed once, verbatim, and counted from one place.

verdict.reasoning: Internal tier, criticality 30, and the record shows convergence rather than a runaway: trend 3, 4, 0, 1 across 4 completed passes, 7 of 8 findings resolved, all 8 in-diff (territory.outsideDiff 0). The single open item (PRRT_kwDOUKOPKc6h_1kx, P2) is that gaps-translation.mjs writes .agents/reviews/pr-<n>/gaps-brief.md and gaps.md without establishing the reviews-directory ignore rule, so a stray generated prompt file can be picked up by `git add -A` -- that is untidy, not critical: nothing in artifact.patch shows a destructive or irreversible action, corruption of the receipt/tracking machinery (gaps-translation.mjs is explicitly non-gating -- "It decides nothing, gates nothing, and refuses nothing"), or a widening of agent authority. Buying a fix costs a write plus the mandatory review round of it under the write-gate rule, at roundsSpent 4 of allowance 5, for a defect whose worst outcome is a committed markdown file a consumer deletes.
gaps: core/scripts/gaps-translation.mjs: neither the `--pr` preview path nor `writeGaps` creates or verifies a .gitignore for .agents/reviews/pr-<n>/, unlike round-translation-page.mjs::writePage, so in a fresh synced consumer the generated gaps-brief.md / gaps.md show as untracked and can be committed by an operator's `git add -A` (Codex, #88 round 4, reproduced in a fresh git repo).

conformance.why: The increment documents `--role gaps-translation` as a runnable command, and without a role definition and schema that command stops in readDefinitionAt() before any reviewer launches -- a real defect in exactly what this change set out to deliver.

The gaps brief generator needs `pr` and `root` and main()'s generic path supplied no `input`, so the documented command threw before dispatch; the fix in core/scripts/fable-dispatch.mjs adds `input: { pr: args.pr, root }` at both call sites.
Collecting gaps from non-terminal `continue` verdicts made the brief report already-repaired defects as shipping, which inverts the one thing the feature exists to tell David correctly.
The paid-for translation landed only in a gitignored JSON receipt while the declared gapsPath had no writer, so the increment's actual product -- prose David can read -- never reached him.

core/docs/ai-context/fable-dispatch.md is the page dispatch() sends a refused caller to, and it stated "Two roles satisfy it" while this diff made three -- a shipped contract contradicting the code it documents.

`split` and `escalate` are not merge decisions, so returning their gaps under a heading saying the PR is shipping with them produces a false brief; the fix pins SHIPPING_VERDICT to ship-with-gaps-recorded alone.

conformance.citation: threatModel.text, agents-core.md: "A choice ... A cheap check that it is well-formed -- non-empty, numeric where a number is expected, a path that exists -- is catching the operator's own mistake, which is exactly the threat model, and stays."
conformance.why: `--pr` is an operator choice and a positivity check is the sanctioned well-formedness kind, not a hostile-value defence -- and the same rule written in two parsers disagreed, with gaps-translation.mjs refusing `--pr 0` while fable-dispatch.mjs accepted it.

The finding is about code this diff introduced (core/scripts/gaps-translation.mjs main() and writeGaps, which mkdir and write into .agents/reviews/pr-<n>/ with no ignore rule established), and no oracle section or threat-model line excludes it -- it is a real if minor defect, which is why it ships as a recorded gap rather than being declined as out of scope.
